meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Vanuatu International Company (VU_IC) under the Vanuatu International Companies Act
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (English common law heritage with indigenous custom law overlay; statutory company and financial services law modeled on Commonwealth practice)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Vanuatu-United Kingdom Double Taxation Arrangement (limited scope)
Vanuatu-Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations (PACER-Plus)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registered Agent licensed by the Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Vanuatu acceded to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention; apostille issued by the Vanuatu Ministry of Foreign Affairs, International Cooperation and External Trade)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified True Copy of Passport (UBO, directors, and shareholders)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in country of issuance or Vanuatu Notary Public; passport verified by licensed registered agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization for non-Hague signatory origin states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuer of original utility/financial statement; certified by notary or licensed agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization depending on origin jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against the Vanuatu FIU consolidated sanctions list, United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list, OFAC SDN list, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, UK HMT sanctions list, and INTERPOL diffusion notices; PEP screening includes domestic and foreign PEPs (at minimum the FATF 2008 definition scope and 2023 FATF amendments), family members and known close associates, with a risk-based enhanced due diligence escalation at 24-hour turnaround; negative news screening across watchlists and adverse media databases; sanctions hit threshold 90% direct match and 85% fuzzy match requiring compliance officer override and VFIU notification within 24 hours where obligation arises under AMLCFT Act s.23-27.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) company name reservation and registration portal (vsc.vu online company registry interface)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory requirement that the company name be expressed in Roman script (Latin alphabet); names in English or Bislama accepted; French-accented characters permitted only if inward transliteration to ASCII is acceptable to the registry; company name must end with the word 'Limited' and may not include the term 'International Company' as a suffix except where necessary to distinguish; the suffix 'IC' or 'I.C.' may be used as part of a custom memorandum election; names must not create confusion with existing registered names, reserved names, or trademarks recorded in the Vanuatu Intellectual Property Office (NSLAPR registry).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Written administrative appeal must be lodged with the VFSC Registrar of International Companies within 14 calendar days of rejection, using Form IC-NAME-APPEAL, stating the grounds of appeal and attaching a legal opinion on the registrability of the disputed name; appeal fee VUV 25,000 (approx. USD 210) payable to VFSC; the Registrar must issue a determination within 15 business days; if the appeal is dismissed, the applicant may apply for judicial review before the Supreme Court of Vanuatu within 30 days; a rejected name may be re-submitted with ministerial endorsement where the rejection arose from a sensitive token requiring prior approval under the International Companies Act s.6(4).

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permitted for the statutory registered office; a physical street address in Vanuatu is mandatory, located at the licensed registered agent's premises; however, the virtual office concept is partially accepted insofar as business records, telephone, and correspondence handling may be outsourced, but the physical registered office must remain at the registered agent's address and the agent must accept service of process; for a trade supply chain factoring company the regulator expects the factoring business operations, including ledger, KYC files, and board minutes, to be maintained at the registered office or at an approved sub-registered address; a pure virtual office with no Vanuatu substance will trigger increased AML risk classification and potential VFSC intervention.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk of unannounced physical on-site inspections is 45% within the first 18 months following licensing, given the VFIU examination cycle for medium-risk trade finance licensees; the risk rises to 70% if the company maintains no directors resident in Vanuatu and relies on a non-resident factoring platform; VFSC conducts statutory on-site examinations under the International Companies Act s.102 and the AML/CFT Act s.76 with notice of 5-10 days, but the compliance manual permits unannounced visits where a systemic risk trigger is identified; the industry benchmark for licensed trade-factoring ICs in Vanuatu is 2 inspections per 5-year supervisory cycle.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act, Cap. 222, Republic of Vanuatu; ss. 7-9 (incorporation by registration), s. 12 (registered office and registered agent), ss. 22-25 (directors and officers), s. 36 (exemptions from taxes).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registry of International Companies, Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC), Port Vila, Vanuatu
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form IC-1 Application for Registration as an International Company, together with the Memorandum and Articles of Association and Statement of Directors
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to an International Company under Cap. 222. Authorised capital is typically fixed at USD 50,000 with nil paid-up at incorporation; no escrow account or capital verification deposit is required under Vanuatu law, although a segregated escrow/SWIFT settlement account is commercially mandated for the cross-border factoring payment rails.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) That the Memorandum and Articles of Association be adopted and filed with the Vanuatu Financial Services Commission for incorporation; (2) That the subscribers' shares be allotted and issued as set forth in the Statement of Share Capital; (3) That the registered office at the registered agent's Port Vila address be adopted for service of process; (4) That the directors and officers named in the Statement of Directors be confirmed in office; (5) That the corporate bank mandate and preliminary trade-factoring contracts be approved. Adopted by unanimous written consent, effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Engagement of Licensed Registered Agent and Name Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: VFSC-licensed Registered Agent (corporate services provider) and Name Reservation Desk, Registry of International Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instructions: Engage a VFSC-licensed registered agent; submit two or three proposed company names ending with 'Limited'; the agent conducts a name-availability search against the International Companies registry and reserves the approved name in writing; no public advertisement is required for a private international company.
required_dossiers: Written engagement letter with the licensed registered agent
Name reservation request listing proposed names
Passport copies of proposed subscribers and directors
Proof of residential address of each subscriber
Consent of registered agent to act as agent for service of process
Completed due diligence questionnaire for beneficial owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or reserved name conflicts, the registered agent files a revised name substitution form with three alternative names within 2 working days; no additional governmental fee is levied for the first resubmission if the originally reserved name was not cited in any public ledger.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of Constituent Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public licensed in Vanuatu or Commissioner of Oaths
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The subscribers and first directors execute the Memorandum and Articles of Association in duplicate; signatures are notarized under wet-ink seal; the notary certifies the Statement of Directors and the consent of the registered agent; the registered office is stated as the registered agent's physical address in Port Vila.
required_dossiers: Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
Notarized Statement of Directors and Officers
Notarized consent of the registered agent
Subscriber declaration of non-resident or resident status
Beneficial ownership declaration form
Power of attorney to the registered agent if remotely executed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the VFSC queries the notarial seal or signature conformity, the notary issues an apostilled Conformed Copy within 5 working days; one free corrective filing is allowed for minor typographical defects in the deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Form IC-1 and Payment of Statutory Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registry of International Companies, Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registered agent submits the completed Form IC-1, the notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association, and the Statement of Directors through the VFSC e-filing portal or in-person counters at Port Vila; the USD 300 registration fee is settled by SWIFT wire from the sponsor bank; the registry stamps the filing receipt and assigns a file number.
required_dossiers: Form IC-1 Application for Registration
Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
Notarized Statement of Directors
Written consent of registered agent
Proof of payment of USD 300 filing fee
Covering letter from the registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a Query Letter, the applicant must respond through the registered agent within 14 calendar days with an Additional Declaration; failure to respond causes the file to be suspended, and rectification requires refiling without loss of original filing priority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Inaugural Corporate Governance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registry of International Companies, VFSC; Board of Directors of the International Company
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon registration approval, VFSC issues the Certificate of Incorporation and enters the company in the public register; the board then convenes its inaugural meeting (or adopts a written resolution), approves the pro-forma first board resolution, issues share certificates, opens the statutory registers, and deposits the minute book and share registers at the registered office with the agent for service of process.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation issued by VFSC
Executed first board resolution
Share certificates issued to subscribers
Register of members
Register of directors and officers
Beneficial ownership register
Statutory minute book
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If VFSC identifies a discrepancy in share allotment or officer details, the company files a Notice of Rectification with supporting board minutes within 10 working days; corrected share certificates are re-issued at nominal cost without loss of incorporation date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Trade-Finance Licensing and AML/CFT Registration for Factoring Operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensing and Policy Division, Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The company submits a finance-license application for the receivables-finance and reverse-factoring line of business, together with a 36-month business plan, AML/CFT policy manual, AML/CFT risk assessment, appointment of the Money Laundering Reporting Officer (MLRO) and Compliance Officer, evidence of the registered office, and confirmation of the segregated escrow/SWIFT settlement arrangement; VFSC conducts fit-and-proper screening of directors and beneficial owners before issuing the operating license.
required_dossiers: Trade-finance (factoring) license application form
Business plan and 36-month financial projections
AML/CFT policy and procedures manual
AML/CFT institutional risk assessment
MLRO and Compliance Officer appointment letters
Due diligence reports on directors, shareholders and beneficial owners
Certificate of Incorporation and Memorandum/Articles
Evidence of registered office and bank mandate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the licensing division issues an intention-to-refuse or requests supplementary information, the applicant submits corrective KYC/AML evidence within 30 calendar days of the decision letter and pays a resubmission fee; an administrative appeal lies to the VFSC Appeals Tribunal within 14 days of the final refusal.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC), Licensing and Policy Division, in coordination with the Ministry of Finance and Economic Management
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Vanuatu Non-Bank Financial Institution (NBFI) Trade-Finance License — Accounts Receivable Factoring and Reverse Factoring Line of Business, subject to AML/CFT registration under the Financial Transactions Reporting Act 2005

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Environmental Protection and Conservation (DEPC), Ministry of Climate Change Adaptation, Meteorology, Geo-Hazards and Energy, Port Vila, Vanuatu
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Environmental Registration (Low Impact Category) — No Full EIA Report required for an office-based factoring operation with no manufacturing, physical processing, or hazard-generating activity
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Nil industrial wastewater or VOC-emitting processes; sanitary effluent only, compliant with Port Vila municipal sewerage by-laws; confidential paper records must be forensically shredded and disposed of under the Waste Management Act manifests; electronic waste and obsolete IT hardware must be surrendered to a DEPC-registered e-waste vendor; any standby generator must comply with WHO/UNEP ambient air-quality thresholds for nitrogen oxides and particulate matter.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate issued by the Vanuatu National Disaster Management Office and Port Vila Fire Brigade following inspection of alarms, extinguishers, and exit signage; structural load inspection certificate for the registered office and secure record/data room under the National Building Code of Vanuatu; NDMO seismic and cyclone-shelter clearance for the leased premises; occupational health and safety clearance under the Vanuatu Health Act for office occupancy.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Vanuatu Revenue Authority (VRA) within the Ministry of Finance and Economic Management, Port Vila. The VRA administers the Value Added Tax Act, Customs Act, and other indirect tax legislation; electronic interface is provided through the Vanuatu Revenue System portal. Company registration for International Companies is administered separately by the Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) under the International Companies Act.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Vanuatu does not operate a general national tax identification number or income-tax registration system. A foreign entity that only holds a Vanuatu International Company (IC) status obtains its corporate identity from the VFSC Certificate of Incorporation and has no automatic income-tax identifier. If the entity nevertheless carries on or intends to carry on a prescribed Vanuatu taxable activity (largely incompatible with IC status), it must submit the standard VAT registration application form to the VRA, accompanied by the certificate of incorporation, constitutional documents, registered office details, banking confirmation, and estimates of taxable turnover. Upon approval the VRA issues a dedicated VAT registration number. A foreign entity that is not registered and does not make taxable supplies in Vanuatu has no statutory obligation to procure a TIN/VAT ID for general inbound trade or offshore factoring activities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box, claw-back, or hybrid mismatch election is available under Vanuatu law. The Vanuatu International Company is automatically and irrevocably tax-exempt for the duration of its valid offshore status. A foreign investor may choose structurally between a local Vanuatu company (which may be subject to VAT registration on local taxable supplies) and an International Company (tax-exempt offshore vehicle), but there is no elective passthrough or entity-level tax election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Vatu (VT) 10,000,000 annual taxable turnover; registration is compulsory once the threshold is met or exceeded and may be voluntary below the threshold in limited circumstances.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Vanuatu does not currently mandate real-time fiscal clearance, e-invoicing APIs, or digital stamping. Registered persons must issue compliant VAT tax invoices, retaining supporting export documentation. The VRA is entitled to require electronic filing of VAT returns through the Vanuatu Revenue System, but no continuous transaction-control or government clearing house requirement applies.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available where the supply qualifies as an export under the VAT Act and the underlying transaction is genuinely offshore or exported. Goods must be exported from Vanuatu in accordance with the Customs Act, with title and effective control passing to a non-resident and the goods physically leaving Vanuatu. Services are zero-rated when supplied to a non-resident recipient for use wholly outside Vanuatu, or where the supply consists of international transport or services directly connected with exported goods. A Vanuatu International Company engaged exclusively in cross-border trade and reverse factoring should not incur local VAT, provided no Vanuatu taxable supply is made and no service is rendered to a Vanuatu resident recipient.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical exportation
Inward Remittance Certificate or foreign exchange credit advice evidencing receipt of export proceeds
Copy of the underlying factoring or trade finance contract
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Zero-rated export claims are subject to retrospective customs and VAT audit. If documentary evidence is insufficient or the alleged export did not occur, the VRA may reclassify the supply as taxable at 12.5% VAT, disallow the refund, impose statutory late-payment interest and civil penalties, and assess additional tax. Knowingly submitting false zero-rating declarations or falsifying export documentation constitutes a criminal offence under both the VAT Act and the Customs Act, potentially exposing responsible officers to fines and imprisonment. In practice, the VRA applies strict evidentiary review to refund claims, and clawback exposure remains open for periods covered by non-filed or fraudulent returns.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of Vanuatu (RBV) under the Reserve Bank of Vanuatu Act [Cap 125], jointly administering the Exchange Control Act [Cap 38] and the Exchange Control Regulations. The Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) separately licenses the factoring entity as a Financial Dealer under the Financial Dealers Licensing Act [Cap 88], while the RBV remains the designated authority for all foreign-exchange, authorized-dealer, and cross-border clearing approvals.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Vanuatu has accepted IMF Article VIII obligations, so current-account payments and transfers are free of exchange-control restriction. The capital account is materially liberalized: a non-resident International Company (VU_IC) may freely receive equity injections, distribute profits, and remit factoring proceeds without prior RBV approval, provided each transaction is routed through an authorized dealer bank (ADB) with an accurate BoP purpose code. The VUV is a managed-float currency with limited offshore market depth and is not deliverable in any major clearing hub; in practice liquidity is cleared in USD, AUD, and EUR. Dividend and profit remittances to non-resident shareholders of an IC are exempt from Vanuatu income tax and withholding tax, leaving exchange-control declaration as the only friction point.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Exchange Control Regulations, resident exporters must ensure that export consideration is remitted to Vanuatu within 6 months of shipment and credited to a foreign-currency account held with an ADB; surplus foreign currency must be offered for conversion into VUV unless the RBV grants a specific exemption. The VU_IC itself is non-resident and therefore not subject to export surrender; however, where it purchases receivables from resident Vanuatu suppliers, the assigned invoice stream must include a contractual warranty that the underlying exporter has complied with the 6-month surrender timeline so that collection proceeds can be routed directly to the VU_IC's escrow account without violation of the RBV regime.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: ANZ Banking Group Limited – Vanuatu Branch
Bank of South Pacific Limited – Vanuatu Branch

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low (restricted). Vanuatu has no local fintech-EMI license category that grants direct access to the national VUV clearing system. Offshore digital EMIs would require a VFSC Financial Dealer Licence and typically cannot secure sponsored settlement accounts at local ADBs. The efficient route is a standard corporate escrow account at a tier-1 ADB combined with the ADB's regional USD nostro clearing capability.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: At least one natural-person director or a duly appointed attorney-in-fact must attend a physical KYC interview at a Port Vila branch of ANZ or BSP when opening the initial corporate account. Remote opening is granted only where (i) the ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) already hold a banking relationship with the same ADB group, and (ii) the bank's compliance officer completes a video-conference KYC call with directors and obtains notarized/apostilled certified copies of passports, proof of address, and the company registry file.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity through bearer shares or unregistered trust ownership of the International Company
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full register of members; signed UBO declaration using the Vanuatu licensed agent's standard form; corporate ownership chart; certified copies of passports; a written statement from the licensed company service provider confirming the economic owner and the source of the subscribed capital

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Factoring program mischaracterized as unlicensed money lending or deposit-taking
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed Master Factoring Agreement with true-sale language; invoice assignment notices; debtor ledger evidencing legal transfer of receivables; express no-recourse or limited-recourse provisions; VFSC Financial Dealer Licence or a licensing-exemption legal opinion addressing the Money Lenders Act [Cap 87]

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering red flags from rapid assignment turnover and high-risk debtor jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Entity-level AML/CFT manual aligned to FATF standards; transaction-monitoring records and at-arm's-length pricing reports; underlying transport documentation (bill of lading, airway bill, customs declarations) for each stored receivable; external-auditor certification of the collateral ledger provided directly to the on-boarding ADB

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Initial capital injections are wired via SWIFT MT103/MT202 from the investor's international bank to the VU_IC's designated USD/VUV escrow clearance account at the onshore ADB. Every transfer must (i) quote a BoP purpose code corresponding to an equity or capital-subscription inflow, (ii) reference the executed share-subscription agreement, and (iii) where the transfer exceeds the ADB's reporting threshold (typically VUV 10 million or equivalent), be accompanied by the RBV exchange-control notification form. VUV-denominated landing is discouraged; the USD account should be used as the primary liquidity anchor and spot-converted only when VUV disbursements are necessary.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Factoring payouts and trade settlements are executed through SWIFT MT103 with full invoice-reference fields, cleared against the ADB's USD nostro lines. Where the underlying transaction involves a matched documentary export, a confirmed, irrevocable sight or usance commercial letter of credit (LC) may be issued through the ADB to the selling supplier, with the VU_IC as LC applicant. Straight MT103 transfers remain the default rail for reverse-factoring prepayments and repayment of assigned receivable collections. All outbound flows must quote the master-factoring agreement number to preserve the audit trail.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/VUV spot contracts with the onshore authorized dealer for immediate settlement of purchase consideration
USD/VUV firm and optional forwards with tenors of 10 to 90 days, quoted by the ADB against a defined invoice-maturity schedule
AUD/VUV and USD/AUD spot or plain-vanilla swap lines to hedge currency mismatch between USD-denominated receivables and AUD/VUV operating costs

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in VUV, permissible only when no onshore deliverable quote is available, and subject to bilateral credit-line margin terms acceptable to the ADB; NDF usage is supplemental and not the primary hedge rail

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return Filing for International Company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of the company's anniversary of incorporation; subject to VFSC extension on application before due date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late penalty of VUV 5,000 (approx. USD 42) after the filing deadline; continued non-compliance for 3 consecutive years may result in administrative strike-off and loss of limited liability status

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Economic Substance Notification / Declared Status Return (where applicable)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) and Vanuatu Revenue & Customs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days of the first annual general meeting date or as prescribed by the International Companies (Economic Substance) Rules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Suspension of corporate registration and daily compounding penalties; repeat default may lead to strike-off; directors subject to personal fines not exceeding VUV 1,000,000 (approx. USD 8,400)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Business License Renewal (where trading in or from Vanuatu)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Vanuatu Department of Customs and Inland Revenue (DCIR) / Municipal Authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 30 April or on the license anniversary date according to the municipal by-laws
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Immediate non-trading restriction and fines under the Business Licences Act; continued lapse beyond 6 months triggers revocation of license and additional restoration costs

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Statement of Beneficial Ownership Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 14 days after the first anniversary of the annual return date; must be updated within 14 days of any shareholding or UBO change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Civil penalties of up to VUV 500,000 (approx. USD 4,200) per false or omissive declaration; custodial liability exposure for directors under the Beneficial Ownership Act 2020

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Audit is not generally mandatory for International Companies under the Vanuatu International Companies Act except where the company is a licensee regulated by the VFSC (e.g., insurance, banking, securities) or holds a financial/factoring license under the International Banking or Captive Insurance regimes
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS is recommended for licensed financial activity; otherwise, the company may maintain simplified statutory records that reflect its financial position with no specified local GAAP requirement; no public financial statements are required for exempt international companies

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: An International Company must keep a register of beneficial owners at the registered office or agent; in the case of an annual shareholding transfer, the company must lodge the updated UBO register with the VFSC within 14 days and submit an annual confirmation in the prescribed form; the register must contain full legal name, residential address, ID/passport details, nature of control, and date of becoming a beneficial owner

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500 - USD 7,500 for a licensed factoring entity requiring a certified independent audit under IFRS

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% (Vanuatu levies no corporate income tax, no capital gains tax, no withholding tax, no payroll tax, and no stamp duty on International Company instruments)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: International Companies (ICs) are tax-transparent in Vanuatu tax law; all offshore income from accounts receivable factoring and reverse factoring is exempt. Local VAT at 12.5% applies only to taxable supplies of goods and services made in Vanuatu; financial services, including factoring and discounting of trade receivables, are exempt supplies. No tax moratorium or preferential deduction regime exists because the baseline effective rate is already nil.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: International Company Annual Return (Form IC-AR) under the International Companies Act 1992 (Cap 191), filed electronically through the Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) Online Registry Portal (www.vfsc.vu) by the licensed registered agent
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within one calendar month after each anniversary of the date of incorporation; no corporate income tax return is required because the IC is tax-exempt. The annual return is the sole statutory recurring filing, and it integrates the annual Economic Substance (ES) declaration.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exact legal name and VFSC company registration number of the International Company
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must match the charter and certificate issued at incorporation; the name must include 'Limited' or 'Ltd.'. Non-resident shareholders must use the same official name in all banking, SWIFT, and escrow documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered office physical address in Vanuatu
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A full street address in Vanuatu served by a VFSC-licensed registered agent is mandatory; a PO Box or email address is not sufficient and will cause rejection of the filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered agent name and licence number
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident directors cannot self-file; the registered agent must sign and submit. Principal place of business outside Vanuatu must be separately disclosed to the agent in writing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Directors and company secretary particulars (full names, residential addresses, nationalities, dates of appointment)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Minimum of one director natural person, any nationality; corporate directors are ineligible under VFSC policy for ICs engaged in financial services. Non-resident directors' identities must be verified under the Anti-Money Laundering rules and their physical address disclosed.

Bearer shares are prohibited. All non-resident controlling shareholders must be disclosed to the registered agent for the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) register; the UBO register is kept by the agent and is not a public document.

No minimum paid-up capital requirement. The authorised capital is stated in VUV, USD, or AUD; annual VFSC government fees are computed in tiers based on this stated authorised capital, which directly affects the factoring entity's operating cost.

Indicate whether the IC carries on a 'relevant activity' under the Economic Substance Regulations. Cross-border factoring and reverse factoring of trade receivables must be classified as a 'financing and leasing' relevant activity. Non-resident entities cannot elect to disregard this classification; failure to declare accurately is a criminal misstatement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Location of accounting records and books of account
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Records may be maintained outside Vanuatu, but the registered agent must state where they are physically located, and VFSC must be able to obtain them within a reasonable period (usually 72 hours on written request). In practice, SWIFT wire confirmations and escrow account statements must be retrievable.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file the annual return on time triggers a monthly late-filing penalty imposed by VFSC, suspension of the certificate of good standing, and administrative strike-off after six months of continued default. VFSC may impose a monetary penalty of up to VUV 1,000,000 for non-compliance under the International Companies Act, with an additional daily penalty for continuing breach. Striking-off results in asset seizure and the impossibility of filing claims in foreign courts.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% — Vanuatu does not impose any withholding tax on dividends paid by an International Company to its non-resident shareholders, and it does not impose a branch remittance tax on distributions from a registered foreign company's Vanuatu branch.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Vanuatu has not entered into any comprehensive Double Taxation Agreement (DTA) with OECD or Asian counterparties; accordingly, no conventional DTA relief application is available for dividend, interest, or royalty flows. The only relevant administrative mechanism is the issuance of a Certificate of Fiscal Residence / Tax Status by the Vanuatu Department of Finance (Revenue and Tax Administration) for a fee, which a parent company may use unilaterally to claim a foreign tax credit in its home jurisdiction under domestic foreign tax credit rules. Because no treaty reduction can be invoked, the protocol is limited to: (1) applying for the certificate with the Department of Finance, (2) submitting the certificate to the foreign revenue authority, and (3) supplementing it with the VFSC annual return and banking evidence. Vanuatu's Tax Information Exchange Agreements (TIEAs) with Australia, New Zealand, and other partners are used exclusively for administrative exchange of information and do not confer any reduced rate of tax.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: 0% withholding tax on interest paid to foreign lenders and 0% on royalty / factoring fee income paid to foreign finance providers. Treaty rates: not applicable (no DTA network). However, the non-resident recipient may be taxed in its own jurisdiction under domestic law, and the factoring entity should certify the beneficial ownership to mitigate double taxation.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No statutory transfer pricing documentation threshold applies in VUV because Vanuatu has no corporate income tax and therefore no TP adjustment mechanism. Notwithstanding, the Economic Substance Regulations impose a qualitative substance threshold on relevant activities. For a factoring entity holding trade receivables and issuing short-term financing against invoices, the annual ES return requires disclosure of: (a) board meeting minutes and quorum held in Vanuatu, (b) physical premises with permanent local staff, (c) senior management physically present in Vanuatu, and (d) total operating expenditure in Vanuatu commensurate with the factoring volume. There is no de minimis revenue threshold; any IC with a relevant activity is captured.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Vanuatu Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) 2020 apply to every International Company engaged in a relevant activity. Factoring and reverse factoring of trade receivables are categorised under the 'financing and leasing' head. The entity must demonstrate: (1) management and control exercised in Vanuatu (at least two board meetings per year physically in Vanuatu, with minutes signed in-country), (2) adequate physical premises and employees proportionate to the factoring book, (3) operating expenditure in Vanuatu proportionate to the income booked, and (4) strategic and operational decisions taken in Vanuatu, including credit risk analysis, funding decisions, and collection supervision. Outsourcing of core functions to a foreign affiliate is permissible only if a local compliance officer supervises and local records are retained. The annual ESR return is filed simultaneously with the VFSC annual return; VFSC may request documentation and levy penalties for non-compliance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Vanuatu IC as a bare special purpose vehicle that merely holds factoring rights and receivables without performing any substantive credit-management, funding, or collection activities from Vanuatu; failing to maintain a local office, local staff, or board minutes in Vanuatu; routinely passing strategic decisions in Hong Kong, Singapore, or Dubai while the IC is presented as a VFSC-licensed factoring principal.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: VUV 5,000,000 financial penalty under the Economic Substance Regulations; a further VUV 100,000 per month of continuing default; mandatory strike-off from the VFSC register; potential referral to the Vanuatu Financial Intelligence Unit, and listing of the entity and its beneficial owners as non-compliant with the OECD Inclusive Framework, which can lead to additional foreign countermeasures.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign a false ESR declaration are personally liable for the penalty up to VUV 5,000,000 and jointly and severally liable for the entity's unpaid penalties; the corporate veil will be pierced if the entity is a façade for the foreign parent; directors may be disqualified for up to 10 years and banned from leaving Vanuatu at the request of the VFSC.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating trade-supply-chain factoring payment rails through escrow accounts and SWIFT wires that accept funds from sanctioned entities, shell importers, or politically exposed persons; using reverse factoring invoices that are fabricated, duplicated, or otherwise used to move proceeds of fraud; deliberately failing to conduct customer due diligence (CDD) on commercial counterparties in the underlying trade transaction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalties under the Financial Transactions Reporting Act and the Vanuatu Proceeds of Crime Act: fines up to VUV 10,000,000 and imprisonment up to 20 years; confiscation of the factoring proceeds and the escrow account balances; revocation of the VFSC licence; freezing of all money held in the Vanuatu banking system.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers are criminally liable if they act recklessly or with intent to facilitate money laundering; the court may impose imprisonment up to 20 years, corporate director disqualification, and travel bans; personal assets traceable to the offence are subject to civil confiscation; the registered agent may also be criminally fined if the agent failed to report suspicious transactions in relation to the factoring portfolio.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Making false declarations in the annual return regarding the nature of the relevant activity; hiding the true beneficial owner of the factoring entity from the registered agent to avoid foreign tax reporting (e.g., FATCA, CRS); mischaracterising factoring fee income as a loan to evade foreign tax; maintaining two sets of invoice-discounting records with local authorities and foreign banks.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Offence under Section 76 of the International Companies Act 1992: fine up to VUV 1,000,000 and/or imprisonment up to 2 years, plus a daily penalty of VUV 10,000 for continuing false certification; VFSC shall cancel the certificate of incorporation; the Attorney General may petition for conditional sanctions; foreign tax authorities may impose secondary penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly authorise a false return face imprisonment of up to 2 years, personal fines, and additional public scrutiny; if the IC is used as a sham to evade foreign taxes, foreign civil courts may pierce the veil and hold directors personally liable for restitution to the defrauded revenue authority; bank accounts held by the director in Vanuatu are subject to freezing orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Conducting accounts-receivable factoring and reverse factoring without maintaining the requisite VFSC licensing as a financial dealer, or accepting deposits from the public disguised as factoring advances; using the ISIC 6492 trade-finance model to operate a deposit-taking scheme that requires a banking licence under the Vanuatu Banking Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Unlicensed financial dealings: monetary penalty of up to VUV 5,000,000 per contravention; VFSC official warning and prohibition order; possible liquidation by court order if the factoring book is exposed; the obligation to refund all affected trade counterparties. Unlicensed deposit-taking activity is a criminal offence punishable by imprisonment as well as fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of an unlicensed factoring business are personally exposed to criminal liability for each day of unauthorised activity, restitution to all defrauded creditors, disqualification under the Companies Act registry, and potential travel bans while the Financial Intelligence Unit conducts the investigation.
